gap.behavioural_impact: In a period format the modern card can be brought back from the Graveyard by Monster Reborn, Premature Burial or Call of the Haunted, and its negation is a chain link that the opponent can respond to or negate instead of a continuous shield that stops the activation and the effects of every Spell/Trap targeting it. Round 036 (2026-09-29): the revival half of this statement is withdrawn; the UDE/Konami card FAQ (Konami-hosted 2008-12-15) says "You can use "Premature Burial" or "Call of the Haunted" to Special Summon "Fushioh Richie" from your Graveyard, as long as "Fushioh Richie" was Special Summoned using the proper method ("Great Dezard") previously.", so the modern card is period-correct there. The negation half stands.

review.notes:
The pinned cards.cdb text matches no lineage version (best match index 1 at ratio 0.4246) because it is an unofficial rendering of the OCG card's functionality; the English lineage stops at DB2-EN229 (2005-07-27), so the divergence cannot be dated from any printing and effective is left empty. Era text at Edison is v1; the GOAT snapshot (2005-04-01) predates v1 and falls on v0 (PGD-031, 2003-07-18), which additionally LACKS the 'This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set' line that DB2 added - whether the PGD printing was actually Normal Summonable in 2005 play is not settled by anything in the packet, which is a second reason this card needs escalation. The remaining v0-to-v1 differences ('offering ... as a Tribute' to 'Tributing', 'Magic or Trap' to 'Spell and Trap', dropping the summoned-position choice) are cosmetic, as is the modern 'target 1 Zombie monster in your GY' for the flip-summon revival. This card has no upstream historical or unofficial variant of any kind.

Round 036 (2026-09-29) class answer applied. The summary said the era wording is a strict nomi that cannot be revived. Konami's rulebook, Versions 7.0 (capture 2008-12-30), 7.1 (2010-03-30), 7.2 (2011-05-16) and 8.0 (linked from Konami's Gameplay page on 2011-09-18), says of Special Summon Monsters: "You cannot use a card effect to Special Summon those monsters from your hand, Deck, or the Graveyard unless it was properly Special Summoned first." Konami's TCG strategy article (printed date 2009-12-07; earliest capture 2015-11-06) says a monster worded "This card can only be Special Summoned by..." can be Special Summoned again from the Graveyard after one proper Summon, and reserves the permanent lock for "cannot be Special Summoned except by...". Konami's Extreme Victory card rulings (compiled 2011-05-12, version 1.2; listed on Konami's Gameplay page on 2011-09-18) rule, for a card whose text is "This card can only be Special Summoned by controlling 3 or more face-up "Meklord" monsters": "If you Special Summon this card correctly, it can later be Special Summoned back from the Graveyard." This card's text says "can only be" and not "except", and the card's own FAQ entry agrees (Konami-hosted 2008-12-15, page F-H: "You can use "Premature Burial" or "Call of the Haunted" to Special Summon "Fushioh Richie" from your Graveyard, as long as "Fushioh Richie" was Special Summoned using the proper method ("Great Dezard") previously."). The same FAQ says "When your opponent uses "Double Snare" on "Fushioh Richie", "Double Snare" is negated and destroyed.", which does not decide the chain-less versus Quick Effect question. The transition stays functional on the negation. Superseded summary, kept verbatim: "Two behavioural differences separate the last English printing (v1, DB2-EN229) from the implemented modern card. First, the strict 'This card can only be Special Summoned from your hand or your Deck by Tributing 1 "Great Dezard" that has fulfilled the condition' became the 'Must first be Special Summoned by "Great Dezard"' form: official/c39711336.lua carries only c:EnableReviveLimit() with no EFFECT_SPSUMMON_CONDITION, so once properly summoned the modern card can be Special Summoned from the Graveyard by anything. Second, the era negation is continuous and chain-less - 'As long as this monster remains face-up on the field, negate the activation and effects of all Spell and Trap Cards that target this card and destroy them' - while the script implements a mandatory Quick Effect (EFFECT_TYPE_QUICK_F on EVENT_CHAINING) that forms its own chain link, answers only card activations (s.discon requires re:IsHasType(EFFECT_TYPE_ACTIVATE)) and only when it sits directly above them (Duel.GetCurrentChain()~=ev+1 aborts), so a targeting effect from an already-resolved or already-face-up Spell/Trap goes unnegated. No English printing carries the modern wording, so the chronology is unresolved and no date is asserted." Evidence and its limits: docs/research/period-rulings-generated-scripts.md, section 3 and the round-036 section. The record's chronology is unresolved (no effective date) and is unchanged.

Round 038 (2026-09-29), part C. The transition carries a full rulings_check, built from the evidence rounds 035 to 037 already held and re-read at the archived captures, so the rulings gate needs no exemption for it. The Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12-15, page F-H) and the 2005 UDE page hold the same entry; nothing read decides whether the era negation was continuous and chain-less or a chain link. Verdict: the remaining difference unresolved at Edison and at Tengu, unchanged. No kind, summary or coverage changed.

event.historical_text: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned from your hand or your Deck by Tributing 1 "Great Dezard" that has fulfilled the condition. You can flip this card into face-down Defense Position once per turn during your Main Phase. As long as this monster remains face-up on the field, negate the activation and effects of all Spell and Trap Cards that target this card and destroy them. When this card is flipped face-up, you can Special Summon 1 Zombie-Type monster from your Graveyard.
event.summary: Functional erratum, narrowed by round 036 to what is still functional: the era negation is continuous and chain-less - "As long as this monster remains face-up on the field, negate the activation and effects of all Spell and Trap Cards that target this card and destroy them" - while the modern script implements a mandatory Quick Effect (EFFECT_TYPE_QUICK_F on EVENT_CHAINING) that forms its own chain link, answers only card activations (s.discon), so the opponent can respond to or negate it. The other difference of the earlier summary is withdrawn: the era "This card can only be Special Summoned from your hand or your Deck by Tributing 1 "Great Dezard" that has fulfilled the condition" says "can only be", not "except", and on Konami's period rulings and the card's own FAQ entry it can be Special Summoned from the Graveyard after that proper Summon, as the modern card can.

rulings_check.difference: The era negation is continuous and chain-less (it stops the activation and effects of every Spell and Trap Card that targets the card); the modern script implements a mandatory Quick Effect that forms its own chain link and answers only card activations, so the opponent can respond to or negate it.
